title: Lockwood Lewis and Cab Calloway's arrival
summary: After front man Lockwood Lewis left, the band hired Cab, who came from the Alabamians and Blackbirds.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: So we had a leader called Lockwood Lewis. He was a formal(?) -looking kind of guy. He didn't move, but he just directed, started the band off... He didn't move much. So I don't know whether Lockwood quit or what...
...was he just a guy that stood in front of the band.
Just some guy that stood in front of the band.

No, he didn't sing. [LAUGHING] He didn't sing. See, they came to New York, and had a guy that led the band. You know, they was trying to copy off the other bands, you know, have a leader. So I didn't know his name. But then Lockwood joined the band, and when Lockwood left, the news got around about Calloway, because Calloway had come to New York with a band...
Yeah. And that band didn't make it. So Cab went and got in a show. So they approached him....
What show did he get in?
It was known as Lew Leslie's Blackbirds...

One of them shows. So they went and approached him to come and front the band. So it was all right with us, because we was just trying to make it. And I didn't have nothin' to say, because I had just got in the band. So Cab came in, and he really put a lot of...I won't say class, but he put a lot of oomph to the band. Because he could dance and throw his hair down and all that stuff, and he could sing, too, you know, which was different -- because the other guys couldn't sing.
